title: Scenes run on the Mac Studio when the worktree says so: run-scene ships the build over rsync, tunnels the automation port over ssh and brings screenshots and logs back, with no agent knowing
description:
User 2026-10-25: instead of TOOL-47's model (agents, worktrees and tickets on the Mac), keep every agent, worktree, ticket, build and test on the Linux machine and use the Mac Studio (acw28@andrews-mac-studio, 96 GB, over Tailscale) only to host scene JVMs. Linux has 14 GB and fits two crawfish scenes; that is the real limit on parallel agents.

The agent must not have to know. The decision lives in the worktree as it is created: a machine-level setting (recorded by `ixd setup`, e.g. `--scene-host acw28@andrews-mac-studio`, in a per-machine config file, never a tracked file) is written by `ixd wt new` into the worktree (an untracked file or the worktree's environment seed), and every ixdar-cli command that starts, drives, screenshots or shuts down a scene reads it. Same commands, same output paths, same exit codes whether the scene is local or remote.

What remote run-scene needs:
1. Ship the build: after the local compile, rsync both modules' target/classes, the dependency jars on the CP file, and the resources/DSL inputs the scene reads to a per-worktree folder on the Mac (delta copies after the first). Scan paths: scans live in ~/crawfish on both machines (IXDAR_DATA_ROOT); map any other absolute local path or refuse with its name.
2. macOS JVM: LWJGL natives for macos-arm64 on the remote classpath (Maven profile/classifier), -XstartOnFirstThread, and start inside the logged-in GUI session (launchctl asuser) so a window can open; the headless path too.
3. Automation: the server stays on localhost on the Mac; ixdar-cli reaches it through an ssh -L tunnel to a local port, so nothing new is exposed.
4. Results back: screenshots, the scene log and any files a route writes land in the worktree's tmp/ as now (copied back after each command that writes them).
5. Lifecycle: the per-worktree scene-pid record (TOOL-28/36) records host and pid; shutdown, the scene limit and `ixd wt cleanup`/land/archive kill remote JVMs and tunnels; nothing is left running on the Mac.
6. Unreachable host: refuse with the reason (ssh error), never silently run locally.

Known difference: the Mac has no MKL (Accelerate/EJML solver), so solver output can differ (MESH-66). Tests stay local. TOOL-47 parts this replaces: the worker setup, ticket-store syncing and Mac-side review; keep land's master push and wt cleanup.
definition-of-done:
1. A fresh worktree on Linux, with the scene host configured, runs `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene <ring scene> --screenshot tmp/x.png` on IMG_4112 with the JVM on the Mac; the screenshot and log are in the local tmp/; ui-state, click and key routes work through the tunnel.
2. shutdown leaves no JVM or tunnel on either machine; wt cleanup/land/archive also clean remote scenes.
3. Without the setting, run-scene is local and unchanged.
4. Unreachable host refuses with a clear message.
5. Python CLI tests for the remote path (ssh/rsync commands mocked).
testing-plan:
1. uv run python -m unittest ixdar_automation_cli.test_cli.
2. Live: run-scene remote on IMG_4112 and fertility, drive it, shut down, check `ssh mac pgrep java` is empty.
3. ixd setup / wt new run and show their output (ai-workspace has no tests).
changes-made: Ixdar (worktree tool-52): new ixdar_automation_cli/scene_host.py (SceneHost). A checkout whose untracked tmp/scene-host.json names a host runs its scene JVMs there: run-scene and launch reach the host first (one ssh that creates ~/ixd-scenes/<worktree>, writes the supervisor script and links the Mac's async-profiler) and refuse with the ssh reason when it is unreachable (exit 8, nothing run locally); after the local build they rsync both modules' target/classes, the module resources, the poms and any checkout file a -D value names (delta copies; include filters because macOS openrsync rejects the /./ marker of --relative), resolve the macos-aarch64 profile classpath once per build (target/CP-macos-arm64: LWJGL natives-macos-arm64, no MKL) and copy its jars to a shared ~/ixd-scenes/m2. The JVM runs under a supervisor sh that refuses a port already taken on the host, records the JVM pid and kills the JVM when the ssh session dies; its output streams into the usual local tmp/logs file and the same ssh tunnels the automation port (-L 127.0.0.1:P:127.0.0.1:P). The scene record (tmp/automation/<ssh pid>.json) carries host, roots and pid file, so the scene limit and every route work unchanged; AutomationClient.call maps absolute path parameters onto the host (checkout, ~/.m2 jars, data root; anything else refused by name), copies back tmp/ and the resources after every POST and maps host paths in answers back to local ones. shutdown and run-scene's teardown kill the JVM on the host when it outlives the timeout and copy back what it wrote (profile.html, jacoco.exec). Headless only: launchctl asuser needs root, so windowed scenes (mesh-viewer) stay local.

ai-workspace (worktree tool-52): ixd setup --scene-host user@machine records the host in ~/.config/ixd/machine.json (checked with one ssh call first; 'local' clears it). ixd wt new writes it into each new Ixdar worktree as tmp/scene-host.json with directory ixd-scenes/<name>. Landing and archiving a worktree now call worktree.stop_scenes before the removal: ixdar-cli shutdown when the worktree has scene records, then an ssh rm -rf of its ~/ixd-scenes folder.

Verified live: remote ring-tool on IMG_4112 (screenshot and log in local tmp/; 15 px differ from the local run's frame) and on fertility kept alive and driven through the tunnel (ui-state, tools, key CTRL+R switched to the ring tool, click drafted a ring, screenshot by relative path); a second launch was refused; shutdown left no JVM on the Mac and no ssh here; a SIGKILL of the local ssh made the supervisor stop the remote JVM; a profiled launch entry and run-scene --profile brought profile.html back; an unreachable host was refused with the ssh error; without the setting the same scene ran locally; stop_scenes stopped a live remote scene and removed its Mac folder. 121 CLI tests pass (5 new).
review-summary: ixdar-cli's run-scene, launch and shutdown now run a worktree's scene JVM on the scene host its tmp/scene-host.json names, shipping the build over rsync and tunnelling the automation port over ssh. Agents stay on the 14 GB Linux machine while scenes use the Mac Studio, with unchanged commands.
